documentSummary.summary: Work Queue is the principal known System serving the Task Assignment and Tracking Project. Current Registry and Google Sheets evidence confirms a registered Apps Script application, a primary Work Queue operational datastore with Tasks, Task_Templates, Settings, Task_Activity, and Location_Task_Map sheets, a separate RES-013 Employees workbook with stable EMP-### identities and assignment/schedule context, and a shared canonical Locations workbook. The System also has partial Inventory integration. Detailed Apps Script source/deployment behavior was not freshly inspected, so current runtime claims remain bounded. No System Identity Entity Record or permanent System ID is created.
documentSummary.confidence: high for semantic placement, current Registry routing, current datastore/shared-data structures, and resolved employee Resource location; medium for detailed runtime behavior not freshly source-code verified

sections.title: 1. Document purpose and authority
sections.contentSummary: Defines the System Summary as the human-readable authority for the current Work Queue System interpretation while preserving separate authority for Project identity, Resources, roadmap direction, implementation evidence, and work history.

sections.title: 2. Relationship to the Task Assignment and Tracking Project
sections.contentSummary: Places Work Queue as the principal known System inside Task Assignment and Tracking and separates the System from the Project, application, datastore, deployment, and other implementation surfaces.

sections.title: 3. Why System Identity remains deferred
sections.contentSummary: Explains why no System Identity Entity Record or permanent System ID is created in this Project Definition pass and records the questions that must be answered before System Identity is formalized.

sections.title: 4. System purpose
sections.contentSummary: Defines Work Queue's current System purpose as the operational mechanism connecting discrete work, structured context, responsibility, state change, completion, history, and downstream effects.

sections.title: 5. Current architecture baseline
sections.contentSummary: Describes the current registered architecture as an Apps Script application over the Work Queue operational datastore plus shared employee, location, Inventory, documentation, and other contextual Resources.

sections.title: 6. Current Work Queue operational datastore
sections.contentSummary: Identifies RES-003 as the primary Work Queue operational datastore, lists its current sheets, and distinguishes it from the separate RES-013 employee/personnel source.

sections.title: 7. Current Tasks model
sections.contentSummary: Documents the current Tasks schema including task identity, creator, status, priority, category, locations, assignee label and stable employee ID, timestamps, completion data, archival state, templates, and holder-related fields.

sections.title: 8. Current Task Activity / history model
sections.contentSummary: Documents the Task_Activity event/history model and observed activity types while preserving open questions about completeness, edit behavior, and reconciliation with current task state.

sections.title: 9. Current task templates
sections.contentSummary: Documents Task_Templates as a current configuration layer for recurring task semantics and holder/inventory-aware completion metadata.

sections.title: 10. Current settings / configuration
sections.contentSummary: Documents current data-configured Settings including APP_VERSION, default priority, completion-note requirement, notification setting, and location cache duration.

sections.title: 11. Current location-to-task mapping
sections.contentSummary: Documents Location_Task_Map as the Work Queue-specific mapping from location types/areas to applicable task templates.

sections.title: 12. Shared Locations / Building Map relationship
sections.contentSummary: Documents the current shared Klinswork_Locations source and the boundary between canonical physical location identity and Work Queue-specific location behavior.

sections.title: 13. Employee / personnel relationship
sections.contentSummary: Documents the resolved RES-013 employee/personnel source, stable EMP-### identities, assignment/schedule context, technical-manual alignment, and Work Queue's boundary from personnel authority.

sections.title: 14. Inventory relationship
sections.contentSummary: Documents the partial but real Inventory relationship, holder-related task/template fields, technical-manual evidence for Inventory_Holder_Event creation, test/fault evidence, and the authority boundary with Inventory Management.

sections.title: 15. Current application behavior supported by evidence
sections.contentSummary: Separates high-confidence current registered/data structures, behavior visible in task/activity history, and behavior supported by the technical manual but not freshly source-code verified.

sections.title: 16. Evidence reconciliation and current uncertainty
sections.contentSummary: Records resolved and remaining evidence issues, including the resolved employee-source location, version-label ambiguity, uninspected Apps Script source/deployment behavior, incomplete full Inventory propagation, and roadmap-evidence limits.

sections.title: 17. Roadmap boundary
sections.contentSummary: Maintains the boundary between the current-state System Summary and the future-state Work Queue roadmap and identifies partial foundations that must not be mistaken for complete roadmap capabilities.

sections.title: 18. Current known limitations
sections.contentSummary: Lists current known System limitations and distinguishes resolved Resource routing from still-unverified runtime and maturity behavior.

sections.title: 19. System Resources
sections.contentSummary: Indexes directly relevant Resource Registry identities including the Work Queue app, datastore, tasks, employee dataset, shared locations, and technical manual.

sections.title: 20. Integration boundaries
sections.contentSummary: Describes current integration boundaries with Scheduling, employee/personnel authority, Building Map / Locations, Inventory Management, and Documentation.

sections.title: 21. Historical interpretation
sections.contentSummary: Defines how historical Tasker/Work Queue terminology and implementation evidence should be preserved without silently converting dated truth into current truth.

sections.title: 22. Current state
sections.contentSummary: Summarizes the current semantic, Registry, data, runtime-confidence, and documentation state of Work Queue.

sections.title: 23. Unresolved questions
sections.contentSummary: Collects unresolved System questions across identity, source/deployment, personnel integration, task lifecycle, Inventory, Locations, templates/configuration, history/reporting, and Documentation Viewer behavior.

sections.title: 24. Next work
sections.contentSummary: Defines creation and validation of the System Summary sidecar as the immediate next step, followed by manifest/Viewer validation, context-naive resume testing, and material Work Unit history.

sections.title: 25. Source and evidence basis
sections.contentSummary: Records the source/evidence basis and interpretation rules used for the current System Summary, including current Registry, Work Queue data, Employees data, Locations data, technical manual, and roadmap evidence.

sections.title: 26. Governing interpretation
sections.contentSummary: Restates the governing System interpretation and the separation among Project, System, application, operational datastore, shared employee and location Resources, integrations, current evidence, roadmap intent, and System Identity.
